summary.text: Sam Liccardo is the Democratic incumbent representing California's 16th Congressional District, which runs from Half Moon Bay and Pacifica through Silicon Valley, including San Jose, Palo Alto and Mountain View. A former prosecutor, San Jose City Council member and two-term mayor of San Jose, he was first elected to Congress in 2024 and sits on the House Financial Services Committee. His campaign materials emphasize housing, lowering the cost of living, and bipartisan legislation.

paragraphs.text: Born April 16, 1970. According to his Ballotpedia survey, he grew up in the district; Ballotpedia lists Bellarmine College Preparatory as his high school.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Georgetown University (1991, per Ballotpedia), and a law degree (1996) and a master's degree in public policy from Harvard (Kennedy School) (1996).

Worked as a prosecutor of sexual assault and child exploitation crimes in the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office and as a federal prosecutor in the Southern District of California. In his Ballotpedia survey he also lists college professor among his past roles.
Elected to the San Jose City Council (District 3) in 2006 and served from 2007 to 2015; won re-election in 2010.

Elected mayor of San Jose in November 2014 and re-elected in 2018, serving two terms. His House website says San Jose committed to carbon neutrality, expanded community-based policing and launched a large rent relief program during his tenure.
Won the open U.S. House seat in November 2024, defeating fellow Democrat Evan Low, succeeding retiring Rep. Anna Eshoo; took office January 3, 2025.

Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and chairs the New Democratic Coalition's Innovation & Technology Working Group; in July 2025 he led the New Dems' Innovation Agenda, according to his House website.
According to his House website, he and his wife, Jessica Garcia-Kohl, a nonprofit leader, live in Saratoga.
